items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: all those guys I worked with. We’d talk about music and different things and invariably someone would say Louis was the guy.

ctx.x: Yeah. As if that’s where things really started.

Right. Well if you go back before then it was the Dixieland guys and it was Louis Armstrong. And all those guys I worked with. We’d talk about music and different things and invariably someone would say Louis was the guy. He made it possible for everyone else. If Bix hadn’t died, where would his career have gone? How influential would he have been to maybe hear him on a more modern recording than some of that old stuff — which is wonderful stuff with Frankie Trumbauer and Chauncey Morehouse on drums. But it was…
Right. It’s kind of a shame because people listen to it and because of the sound of it it’s easy to sort of dismiss. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
